candidates.title: Draft logistics event notifications

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a draft alert or daily logistics report from operator-supplied shipment and order events.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed, copy an order update into a CRM, alert a buyer when inventory drops, or send a daily report to a team channel.

ease.reason: A synthetic rule-and-alert mock is approachable, but no attached source documents event intake or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: ecommerce operations teams may value delay alerts; this discussion establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic alert draft is bounded; carrier data access and live delivery are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed draft can repeat a rule check, but a person must approve and send each message; no execution is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained task span lists examples but gives no recurrence, input fields, or corroborating demand.

experimentPlan.output: A draft shipment-delay alert or daily logistics summary from supplied event rows.
inputs: Synthetic shipment ID, expected date, and current status
Synthetic order ID and update text
Operator-selected alert rule and recipient role
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a new shipment or order event row for review.
steps: Validate required fields and flag missing values.
Compare the supplied status and date with the operator-selected rule.
Draft a concise alert or daily summary from matching rows.
Show the source rows beside the draft for operator review.
Require a person to approve and send any message.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a small synthetic set, every matching event appears once, nonmatching events are excluded, and each draft matches its input row.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies accurate events and rules, checks every draft, and sends it; no live logistics system or message delivery is established.
unverified: No implementation reference documents event intake or delivery.
Carrier data access, rule correctness, and live notification are unverified.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a narrow proposed experiment; provisional mean is below the threshold of 6 because demand is single-post and implementation is unverified.

candidates.title: Organize game-test CSV logs

demandEvidence.chore: Organize mobile game-test observations from a phone log and CSV into a Google Sheet while avoiding missed or repeated files.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I have tried a Schedule Trigger plus Google Drive Watch Files and also a Webhook from a shortcut on the phone, but the workflow either doesn’t fire at all or fires twice on the same file.

ease.reason: A table mock is approachable, but no attached source documents CSV parsing or deduplication.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: game-testing contractors might value cleaner logs; this one post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic table test is scoped, while reliable parsing and file intake remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed checklist can flag possible repeats, but a human must import and verify; no workflow execution is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe the manual log and repeated or missed file triggers, but provide no corroborating demand.

experimentPlan.output: A checked table of supplied game-test observations, with suspected duplicate files flagged for review.
inputs: Synthetic battery percentage, temperature, and frame-drop values
CSV file name and upload time supplied by an operator
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator provides a sample CSV export or a row of fictional game-test observations.
steps: Read the supplied rows without connecting to a phone or Drive.
Check required columns and flag missing values.
Compare file names and row keys to identify possible repeats.
Prepare a normalized table for a sample sheet.
Ask a person to verify flagged rows and perform any import.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a labeled synthetic CSV set, the output preserves each expected observation, flags planted repeated file keys, and reports missing fields without inventing values.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A tester supplies fictional or authorized test data and confirms each flagged duplicate; the proposal does not control a phone, execute n8n, or write to Sheets.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports CSV parsing, phone upload, or deduplication.
Correct duplicate keys and reliable file-trigger behavior remain unverified.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a narrow proposed experiment; provisional mean is below the threshold of 6 because demand is single-post and implementation is unverified.

candidates.title: Prepare booking exception summaries

demandEvidence.chore: Review operator-supplied booking records for conflicts and draft a human-reviewed exception summary.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Booking flows: check slots, confirm, remind, no double-bookings

ease.reason: A synthetic exception list is a modest prototype, but no source supports booking-check mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small appointment businesses may pay for fewer booking errors; the service listing proves no buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare supplied slots, but calendar access and availability rules are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposal can draft flags for review; a person must verify and contact customers because no booking execution is documented.

evidence.reason: The source advertises booking checks but gives no concrete case, repeated demand, or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A draft list of possible booking conflicts and missing confirmation details.
experimentPlan.trigger: A small batch of synthetic booking rows is supplied for a conflict review.
steps: Check that required booking fields are present.
Compare requested and confirmed slots against the supplied availability rule.
Flag possible overlaps or missing confirmations.
Draft a short exception summary with the relevant row identifiers.
Require a person to verify availability and contact any customer.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: In a labeled synthetic set containing known overlaps and missing confirmations, every planted case is flagged and no clean case is marked as a confirmed conflict.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A business operator supplies permitted test records and authoritative availability rules, verifies every flag, and confirms bookings; no calendar or live customer connection is documented.
unverified: No assigned implementation reference supports booking checks or reminders.
Availability rules, calendar access, and reliable duplicate prevention remain unverified.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a narrow proposed experiment; provisional mean is below the threshold of 6 because demand is single-post and implementation is unverified.

candidates.title: Prepare form responses for a Sheets review

demandEvidence.chore: Connect Google Forms responses to Google Sheets as a small automation task.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Connecting Google Forms to Google Sheets

ease.reason: A student can test fictional form responses and expected rows, but no supplied reference documents Forms or Sheets integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small professional service operators may pay to reduce manual form transfer; this single listing establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can map sample answers into reviewed rows; actual Make execution, field mapping, and persistence are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed mapping is repeatable, but a person must check each row and handle exceptions; no integration execution is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained post explicitly offers Google Forms-to-Sheets connection help, but gives no task details, recurrence, or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A draft Sheets-style row for each supplied sample form response, with missing answers flagged.
inputs: Fictional form response with three labeled answers
Expected row for each fictional response
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies one fictional form response for a mapping review.
steps: List the supplied answer labels and values.
Map each answer to an operator-selected destination column.
Flag missing or extra fields without guessing values.
Prepare a draft row and show its source answers beside it.
Ask a person to verify the mapping before any manual entry.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For labeled fictional responses, every supplied answer appears in its expected column, missing values are flagged, and no output row is presented as saved to Sheets.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person provides authorized test examples and column names, checks the proposed mapping, and performs any real connection or write; no Make execution or external endpoint is established.
unverified: Make Forms trigger behavior and Google Sheets write capability are undocumented in the supplied sources.
Field mapping reliability, permissions, and live persistence are untested.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a proposed mock mapping experiment; provisional mean is 4.8, below threshold, because implementation and buyer evidence are limited.
